title: My calm bedtime routine
group: LDS-FOCUS — Focus and Getting Things Done
examples: How do I get ready for bed?
What is a good bedtime routine?

explain.say: Your body is like a little car. At night, it needs to slow down and park. A bedtime routine is how it slows down. Look at the board. Here are the steps, one at a time.

steps.label: Screens off

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a calm bedroom at bedtime. Look at the bed, the lamp and the clock. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
See the phone light up? Screens off first. Bright screens tell your brain it is daytime. When they sleep, your brain starts to feel sleepy too. Can you switch your screen off before bath time?

explain.say: Now look at the bath. A warm bath or wash. Warm water helps your body relax. Then pyjamas on, soft and comfy, and brush your teeth. How many steps have we ticked now?

explain.say: See the book? Story time. Read or listen to a calm story. Your body is nearly parked. Then lights low, close your eyes, and rest. What is your favourite bedtime story?

explain.say: Look at this clock. Half past seven. If you start your routine at the same time each night, your body learns when to get sleepy. Brilliant work! Here is a challenge. Choose your start time with a grown-up.

faq.q: Why turn screens off before bed?
faq.a: Bright screens make your brain think it is still daytime. Turning them off early helps you feel sleepy sooner.

faq.q: What if I cannot fall asleep?
faq.a: Lie still and take slow belly breaths. Picture a calm place, like a beach. If it keeps happening, a grown-up you trust can help.

faq.q: Why do the same steps every night?
faq.a: When the steps are the same, your body learns that sleep is coming. It is like a signal.

faq.q: What if the routine changes, like on a holiday?
faq.a: Keep as many steps as you can, like teeth and a story. A grown-up can help you make a holiday list.

faq.q: What time should I go to bed?
faq.a: Every family is different. Ask a grown-up to choose a time with you, and put a clock picture on your list.

facts: Bright light from screens in the evening can make it harder to feel sleepy.
Children of primary school age usually need about 9 to 12 hours of sleep each night.

quiz.say: What is a good first bedtime step?
quiz.show: What is a good first bedtime step?
quiz.why: Screens off helps your brain start to feel sleepy.

wrong.1: Fast games wake your brain up.
wrong.2: A big snack late can make it harder to settle.

quiz.say: The clock shows half past seven. How is that written?
quiz.show: Half past seven is written as?
quiz.why: Half past means 30 minutes after the hour, so 7:30.

wrong.1: 7:00 is seven o'clock, not half past.
